Ben / Marissa — I reviewed the sample trace.

Short summary: during the rolling upgrade the node agent appears to terminate the inference worker process before the control plane channel (agent->conductor) completes reconnect. On a subset of nodes the conductor's relay sockets were closed while the agent attempted to re-register, which caused retries and a prolonged backoff (90–150s) before reestablishing the KV cache and prefix routing. This matches an orchestrator restart-order race we've seen once before (INF-7891).

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
- Abort any further rolling restarts on the customer's fleet (pause the job)
- Push a temporary orchestration-level change that forces agent shutdown to wait for control socket teardown confirmation (small change in supervisor ordering) — safe hotfix, can be rolled in <2 hours if we have customer approval
- If customer prefers, roll back to agent 0.8.7 on affected hosts (this avoids the new restart behavior) — rollback is invasive and will require coordination/brief maintenance window

I'll prepare the patch and a short runbook for the ops team. Attaching error traces and a small replication script.

—Aditya
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Attachments: error-traces-05010.zip, replication-script.sh

Subject: Post-incident update & remediation steps — private-node rolling upgrade (timeline & evidence)

Hi Priya / Luke —

Thanks again for raising this. Attached is a short post-incident draft that summarizes our findings, the evidence we've collected, and the remediation steps we propose. TL;DR:

- Root cause: orchestrator restart-order race during rolling upgrade (agent shutdown ordering) caused control-plane reconnect to back off for ~90–150s on a subset of hosts
- Impact: intermittent request failures and retries for two Cedar Health services for ~12 minutes total; peak error rate at 18:17 PDT
- Immediate actions taken: paused the rollout at 18:52 PDT; collected full traces; initiated hotfix work and prepared rollback plan
- Next steps (please confirm preference):
   1) Apply our hotfix (supervisor ordering change) to your staging fleet tomorrow at 02:00 UTC for validation; if validated, schedule a controlled production rollout with canary nodes and a 10-minute monitoring window
   2) If you prefer rollback, we can coordinate a rollback this evening; it requires a 30-minute maintenance window across the fleet

We've included the raw traces (error-traces-05010.zip) and the postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-cedarhealth.pdf). Also linking the internal runbook and the JIRA for the hotfix: https://drive.redwood.com/d/cedar-postmortem-20260510 and JIRA-INF-7891.

As a gesture of goodwill we're offering a one-day usage credit for the affected service hours while we work through remediation — I'll confirm details with your procurement contact if you accept.

Please let us know which remediation path you prefer and whether we have permission to run the hotfix on a small canary cohort tonight for quicker validation.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take these seriously and will prioritize stabilizing your fleet.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
